Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with a distal radius wrist fracture confirmed on
imaging and consistent with the fall-and-impact mechanism described. Physical examination findings, including
localized tenderness, swelling, and restricted range of motion, correlate closely with the radiographic findings. Initial
management consisted of immobilization and analgesia, followed by a structured course of supervised physcial
therapy and home exercise instruction. Over 27 visits, treatment progressed in a typical pattern, with visit frequency
tapering as grip strength, mobility, and pain improved. Rceords also note a minor wrist strain several years prior that
resolved completely without lasting limitation. Billed services reflect the treatment delivered, with no duplicate or
repeated charges identified. At the most recent visit the patient was discharged with good functional recovery and
was advised to return if symptmos recur.
